target_customer: B2B sales teams, from founder-led sales to revenue operations, who run live calls on Zoom, Meet or Teams
problem: Reps lose deals in the moment on live calls because they do not know what to say next or how to answer objections, and top performer knowledge is not reused.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a free tier and paid plans (prices not published on the site)
product_category: Real-time sales copilot and conversation intelligence

founders.name: Swan Beaujard
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists the title and no background, education or prior employers.

founders.name: Ethan Safar
founders.role: Co-founder (title not stated by the YC page)
founders.background_notes: The Hacker News launch post of 2025-05-26 (item 44098706) opens 'Hey HN, we're Swan and Ethan, and we're building heynomi.com' and was submitted by the account ethansafar, and a team comment mentions a solid infra and sales engineering background. The post does not use the word co-founder. The Round Funded page for Nomi names only Swan Beaujard as founder and does not mention Ethan Safar. Product Hunt lists him as co-founder and CEO, a conflicting title that is recorded here as unconfirmed.

competitors.name: Cluely
competitors.what: Real-time AI assistant for calls and meetings, described by a commenter on the Nomi launch thread as aimed at individuals in on-demand situations

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs low-latency live transcription and suggestion generation on top of video call software, plus CRM syncs. Standard speech and LLM components made this feasible for a small team in 2025, but latency and relevance are hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Playbooks built from a team's own calls and CRM integrations add some lock-in, but the underlying transcription and LLM stack is available to every competitor and call recorders could add live prompts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing what incumbents did. Conversation intelligence vendors were already adding AI features in 2025 but I found no dated evidence of a direct copy.

market_need_then: Launch-day discussion shows interest in live call assistance and the founders claim 30 teams were using it at the May 2025 launch (self-reported). The site claims a 12 percent average lift in closing rates, which is unverified.

branding.domain_note: The company site is nomi.so, not a .com. Other companies named Nomi exist, including an AI companion app and a health payments company, which makes the name confusable. No source describes how the domain was obtained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and action focused (headline: Win the moment when it matters)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, no mascot or community found. A search turned up only trademark records and unrelated brands sharing the name.

outcome_analysis: Nomi is a Spring 2025 YC company that launched a real-time sales copilot in May 2025 and is listed as Active with a team of five. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Public funding data is thin and conflicting, so no outcome can be assessed yet, and the main risk visible from sources is a crowded field of call assistants and conversation intelligence vendors.
notes: Unverified funding from aggregators only: about 500K USD pre-seed or convertible note with Y Combinator named as investor (FundedIQ says April 2025, CB Insights says a 0.5M convertible note on 2025-06-18, AngelBacked says 500K pre-seed 2025-04-07 with angel investors). StartupHub lists 180M total, which is almost certainly wrong. No press release or company post confirms any round, so none is recorded. The YC launch page lists the founding year as 2018, which looks like an error. Welcome.ai names a different co-founder, which conflicts with YC. Ethan Safar: the Hacker News launch post treats him as one of the two founders ('we're Swan and Ethan') but the cited Round Funded page does not name him, so the formal co-founder title rests on the launch post wording and Product Hunt. Company site fetched successfully.
